digest.definition: Public Policy and Public Administration are joined but separate: policy studies what shapes the decisions of governments and regulators, administration studies how policy is formed and put into effect
distinctiveFeatures: Public Policy and Public Administration are joined but separate: policy studies what shapes the decisions of governments and regulators, administration studies how policy is formed and put into effect

The subjects study systems, processes, governance and management of public decisions at every tier of government, in democratic and non-democratic states, including the effects of decisions on citizens
They are taught in many host disciplines, among them economics, politics, social policy, sociology, planning, management, law and business

Study follows the policy cycle from problem definition and agenda-setting through design, transfer, instruments and implementation to evaluation, using several theories and comparisons across sectors and systems

Fairness and social justice are central, including the UK public sector equality duty, and principles such as legality, accountability, proportionality and impartiality frame the judgement of public bodies
The subjects are interdisciplinary, join theory with practice and stress effectiveness, efficiency and equity in service design, with co-design, co-production and collaboration between agencies
Public and social value, public service motivation and ethos are characteristic themes; courses are often taught with practitioners and use real cases
Most provision is postgraduate (MSc, MPA, MPP), with pre- and post-experience cohorts; undergraduate Public Administration degrees are few, and public sector content is common in foundation degrees

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: equity is part of the subject matter: fair policy, just institutions and the public sector equality duty; EDI in curriculum, pedagogy and assessment, voices of subjugated groups, inclusive feedback and advisory input (D1, 1.6, 1.12 to 1.14, 3.13)

graduates will design accessible services beyond legal compliance; courses make reasonable adjustments, accessible spaces, resources, visits and careers support, and digital inclusion (D1, 1.15 to 1.17, 3.6, 3.11)
the subject equips future public managers and policymakers to realise the sustainable development goals; ESD pedagogies and UNESCO learning objectives; SDGs among the subfields (D1, 1.18, 1.19, 3.3)

named employability, entrepreneurship and enterprise education (EEE): practice links required for pre- and post-experience students, graduates able to articulate their skills, employer work and accreditation routes (D1, 1.20 to 1.25, 3.10)
degrees must respond to an AI-shaped labour market and changing assessment; ethical, responsible use of GenAI, including in authentic assessment (D1, 1.26 to 1.28, 3.8, 3.12)

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.about: skills that prepare graduates for many occupations
statements.paraphrase: The subject gives students skills, knowledge and capabilities for work in democratic or non-democratic settings marked by uncertainty; courses teach strategic problem-solving and how to hold governments to account, and the skills graduates gain will ready them for many occupations, not only careers in the field.

forPractitioner.text: Teach strategic problem-solving and accountability so that the skills and attributes graduates gain will fit them for a wide range of jobs, including those outside policy and administration.

forBeneficiary.text: The skills and qualities you build will prepare you for many kinds of work, whether or not you go on to a career in public policy or administration.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: critical evaluation of policy and public sector performance
statements.paraphrase: With public sector jobs making up about a fifth of the UK economy and delivery spreading to non-profit and private bodies, investment in public staff matters; degrees will encourage students to evaluate policy critically and to weigh how effective and productive the public sector is.

forPractitioner.text: Design learning so that students will critically evaluate policy and judge the effectiveness and productivity of the public sector, given its size and its growing reliance on non-profit and private delivery.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be encouraged to judge policies critically and to weigh how well and how productively the public sector works.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses
statements.about: EDI in delivery and curriculum
statements.paraphrase: Because the subject serves fair policy and just institutions, its activities should be guided by EDI principles: degrees should observe, build in and advance EDI in teaching and curriculum, and equality, equity, diversity and inclusion should run through knowledge, pedagogy, curriculum, assessment and inclusive learning communities.

forPractitioner.text: Embed EDI in both what you teach and how you teach it: let it shape the curriculum, pedagogy and assessment, and build a subject community where every student and member of staff belongs.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses
statements.about: EDI in academic and administrative practice
statements.paraphrase: EDI should lead academic, teaching and administrative practice in the subject, through inclusive language and through teaching and assessment that acknowledge unequal power, bring in diverse views, advance social justice and create inclusive places to learn.

forPractitioner.text: Put EDI first in day-to-day practice: use inclusive language, choose teaching and assessment that address unequal power and invite diverse views and keep learning spaces inclusive.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: graduates' role in accessible, inclusive services
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will play a central part in shaping policy and services in fields from health and technology to innovation, finance and crises, going beyond legal compliance to provision that is accessible, inclusive, transparent and effective and lets everyone take part.

forPractitioner.text: Prepare students for the part graduates will play in shaping policy and services in areas like health, technology and crisis management, so that they design for full accessibility and participation, not only for legal compliance.

forBeneficiary.text: You will play a central part in shaping policies and services, in areas such as health, technology and crisis management, and in making them open to everyone, beyond what the law demands.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and especially Public Administration degrees, pre- and post-experience
statements.about: links to enterprise and equipping experienced students
statements.paraphrase: Because the subject is closely tied to practice, its degrees for students before and after work experience must link content clearly to enterprise and entrepreneurship, and must give students already in the sector the knowledge, behaviours and skills to grow and advance at work.

forPractitioner.text: Make the link between content and enterprise explicit, and design for experienced practitioners as well as new entrants: they must leave with what they need to progress in their workplace.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.about: recognising and communicating enterprise and employability skills
statements.paraphrase: Graduates understand the worth of the enterprise and employability skills they built during study; courses can deepen that understanding, and students will be able to recognise these skills, reflect on them, develop them and explain them to employers and other stakeholders.

forPractitioner.text: Give students repeated chances to name, reflect on and build their enterprise and employability skills, so that graduates will be able to explain them to current and future employers.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to recognise the enterprise and employability skills you have built, reflect on them, keep developing them and explain them clearly to employers.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Public Policy and Public Administration degree

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses
statements.about: responding to generative AI in teaching and assessment
statements.paraphrase: As AI reshapes the labour market and work alongside smart machines, degrees in the subject must recognise and respond to the needs of employers and workplaces and to changing teaching, assessment and feedback, so that students study responsibly and with integrity; course developers look past assessment security to bring GenAI into wider learning and authentic assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Treat generative AI as a curriculum matter, not only an integrity risk: align with what employers and workplaces need, adapt teaching, assessment and feedback and consider building GenAI into activities and authentic assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: public and social value in courses
statements.paraphrase: Courses also study multilevel governance and how structure, systems and agency interact in the public sector, such as the state's part in policy and the experience of frontline staff; they will also stress public and social value as typical of the field, with public service motivation and ethos as common themes.

forPractitioner.text: Cover multilevel governance and the interplay of structure, systems and agency, and make public and social value a visible thread, alongside public service motivation and ethos.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course will give weight to public and social value, and you will look at how governance works across levels and how frontline staff experience the public sector.

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: progression through the honours levels towards the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Over an honours degree (FHEQ level 6; FQHEIS level 10) students will progress level by level under each institution's rules, each level adding knowledge, expertise and experience towards the threshold subject and generic skills; this will usually mean completing all learning and assessment for credit, practical parts included, and a graduate with a second-class degree or better would be expected to be ready for postgraduate study, though providers set entry rules.

forPractitioner.text: Plan each level so that it builds knowledge, expertise and experience towards the threshold subject-specific and generic skills by graduation, with credit earned across all learning and assessment, practical work included.

forBeneficiary.text: As you move through each year of your honours degree, you will build the knowledge, expertise and experience that lead to the minimum standard by the end, completing all your learning and assessment, practical work included. With a second-class result or higher you would usually be ready for postgraduate study, though each university sets its own entry rules.

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.about: joint and combined degrees
statements.paraphrase: Undergraduates taking the subject in a joint or combined degree will reach the core of its specific and generic skills and add others from their other subject, and may explore where disciplines overlap.

forPractitioner.text: In joint or combined honours, make sure students will still attain the core subject-specific and generic skills of this statement, while the partner subject adds its own.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study this subject as part of a joint or combined degree, you will gain its core subject and general skills and add others from your second subject.

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.about: skills for policy, management and leadership across sectors
statements.paraphrase: Graduates are expected to be equipped to work well as policymakers, managers, leaders and agents of change across public, private and non-profit sectors; public service and public administration are distinct professions whose members can move between policy and administration, and students will be helped to see that services are delivered through multi-agency models where cross-sector working is normal.

forPractitioner.text: Build skills for policymaking, management, leadership and change across sectors, and teach that services are delivered by multi-agency partnerships, so that graduates will have what they need to move between policy and administration roles.

forBeneficiary.text: You will gain the skills to work as a policymaker, manager, leader or change agent in public, private or non-profit organisations, and you will learn how services are delivered by many agencies working together.

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.appliesTo: degree-awarding bodies and their collaborative partners
statements.about: the student voice in monitoring and review
statements.paraphrase: Degree-awarding bodies and their partners routinely gather and analyse information and review degrees periodically, and the student voice will form part of this; they use external reference points, this statement among them, and evaluation can include regular review of EDI in the learning community.

forPractitioner.text: Include students' views in routine monitoring and periodic review, use external reference points and consider reviewing EDI within the learning community as part of evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the awarding body; students take part in review but do not reach it as a standard

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.about: external reviewers in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Externality is a core part of UK quality assurance: providers will use external reviewers in periodic review to bring an outside view of proposed changes, check that threshold standards are met and confirm that content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Bring external reviewers into periodic review to test proposed changes, confirm that threshold standards are achieved and check that the content fits the subject.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Distinctive features of Public Policy and Public Administration degrees

statements.appliesTo: courses with professional or vocational outcomes evaluated by accrediting bodies
statements.about: integrating accreditation requirements
statements.paraphrase: Courses whose professional or vocational outcomes are evaluated by professional and accrediting bodies will need to build those requirements into how the degree is managed.

forPractitioner.text: Where professional or accrediting bodies evaluate the course, build their requirements into degree management from the start.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: practice-based learning
statements.paraphrase: Students will usually learn how policy making, public administration and decision making have developed through practice-based learning, working on real problems and building critical skills through approaches such as action learning and reflection and through placements in public and non-governmental bodies.

forPractitioner.text: Use practice-based learning: real-world problems and action learning with reflection, plus focused placements in public and non-governmental organisations.

forBeneficiary.text: You will usually learn through practice: working on real problems, reflecting on what you do and perhaps taking a placement in a public agency or a non-governmental organisation.

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: engagement with governance and policy across contexts
statements.paraphrase: Degrees introduce the design and running of governments and of the public and voluntary sectors; no sector or institution is essential, but study will include close engagement with questions of governance and policy, applying theories, concepts, values and principles across many contexts; all students study the public sector conceptually and empirically at every tier of government, and typically know a number of the listed subfields.

forPractitioner.text: Choose any sectors or institutions, but make sure students engage closely with governance and policy questions, apply theory across contexts from the individual to the global and study the public sector both conceptually and empirically, drawing on several of the listed subfields.

forBeneficiary.text: You will study how governments and the public and voluntary sectors are designed and run, apply theories and principles to real questions of governance and policy in many settings and get to know several specialist areas of the field.

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses
statements.about: learning environments and digital inclusivity
statements.paraphrase: Each provider's learning and teaching will reflect its own approach to the subject; methods fit the subject matter, the outcomes and learners' needs, embrace sustainability, inclusion, diversity, accessibility and enterprise, recognise students' prior learning cultures and the global context, and run across many modes; and providers will make digital learning inclusive wherever they can.

forPractitioner.text: Fit teaching methods to the content, outcomes and learners, build in sustainability, inclusion, accessibility and enterprise, use a mix of modes and do what you can to make digital learning inclusive for every student.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: a range of learning environments and methods
statements.paraphrase: Students will meet a mix of learning settings, methods and activities that together build cognitive and life skills and knowledge and help them find enterprising answers to social challenges; whatever the mode, learning typically combines several of the listed methods.

forPractitioner.text: Offer a varied mix of settings and methods that build cognitive and life skills and enterprising responses to social challenges, drawing on lectures, seminars, case studies, simulations, placements, independent study, practitioner talks and fieldwork.

forBeneficiary.text: You will learn in many ways, such as lectures, seminars, case studies, simulations, placements, guest talks and field trips, which together build your thinking, your life skills and your ideas for tackling social problems.

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses
statements.about: an assessment strategy aligned with curriculum and outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Assessment and feedback help students engage deeply and show their understanding, analysis, insight and skills; a course's assessment strategy will mirror the knowledge, skills and understanding in its curriculum and fit its teaching methods, with assessment for and as learning, tied to learning outcomes, showing rising attainment and building employability and professional skills.

forPractitioner.text: Align the assessment strategy with the curriculum and teaching, link each task to stated outcomes, use assessment for and as learning and let it show progression and build employability and professional skills.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course's assessment design; the student meets its effect

statements.appliesTo: Public Policy and Public Administration courses and their students
statements.about: constructive feedback throughout study
statements.paraphrase: Feedback is central to learning and helps students see their progress and improve; it will be constructive, consistent and specific, and will come throughout study on formative and summative work so that students can carry it forward; varied methods, from written and spoken comments to technology and peer and self-assessment, support equality and inclusion.

forPractitioner.text: Give constructive, consistent and specific feedback on formative and summative work across the course, timed so that students can use it on later tasks and vary its form for a diverse cohort.

forBeneficiary.text: You will get feedback that is constructive, consistent and specific on both practice and marked work throughout your studies, so that you can use it on your next tasks.

statements.about: using Annex D for classification
statements.paraphrase: Most students will perform well above the minimum threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows this and should use Annex D of the 2024 Frameworks, the classification descriptions for FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10 degrees, which describe the four honours classes and postgraduate outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Decide how your institution evidences performance above threshold, and use Annex D of the 2024 Frameworks, the classification descriptions for honours at FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10, when setting class boundaries.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.about: competence standards and EHRC guidance
statements.paraphrase: The minimum threshold standards are not universal competence standards; a provider that writes competence standards under the Equality Act 2010 into a programme specification may draw on this statement and any PSRB requirements, and should follow the Equality and Human Rights Commission's latest guidance.

forPractitioner.text: If you write competence standards (Equality Act 2010) into a programme specification, you may draw on this statement and PSRB requirements, but follow the latest EHRC guidance and do not treat the threshold standards as competence standards.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the people who design and run it, not a standard the student reaches

statements.about: key concepts, theories and current evidence
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Shows knowledge of the subject's main concepts and theories and an awareness of the evidence now available.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show that they know the field's core concepts and theories and are aware of current evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will show that you know the main concepts and theories of public policy and administration and are aware of current evidence.

statements.about: current problems and new insights near the forefront
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Shows knowledge, understanding and awareness of present problems or fresh insights, much of it drawn from or shaped by leading work in the discipline or in professional practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show knowledge and understanding of present problems or new insights, much of it shaped by leading research or professional practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will know and understand today's problems and new thinking in the field, much of it drawn from leading research or practice.

statements.about: building an argument with judgement
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can build an argument, bringing relevant information together and using judgement.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can build an argument that draws relevant information together and uses judgement.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will build an argument that brings together the relevant information and shows your own judgement.

statements.about: complex issues and judgement with incomplete data
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can handle complex issues in an orderly and inventive way and reach sound judgements when data are incomplete.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can handle complex issues methodically and inventively and judge soundly when information is missing.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will handle complex issues methodically and inventively, and reach sound judgements when some of the information is missing.

statements.about: problems in practical and theoretical contexts
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can find, look into and resolve problems in both practical and theoretical settings.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can find, examine and resolve problems in practical and theoretical settings.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will spot, look into and resolve problems, in practice as well as in theory.

statements.about: approaches to collecting, analysing and presenting data
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can judge and use suitable ways of gathering, analysing and presenting relevant data.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can assess and use methods for gathering, analysing and presenting relevant data.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will choose and use good ways to gather, analyse and present the data a question needs.

statements.about: collaboration towards shared goals
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Works with others towards shared aims, for instance in group tasks, projects and presentations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates work with others towards shared aims, for example in group tasks, projects and presentations.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will work with others towards shared aims, for example in group work, projects and presentations.

statements.about: communication in varied formats and for varied audiences
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Communicates in formats suited to the context and to different audiences.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates communicate in formats that suit the context and different audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will communicate in forms that suit the setting and the people you are addressing.

statements.about: reflection on own learning
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Reflects on their own learning.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates reflect on their own learning.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will think about how you are learning and what that tells you.

statements.about: managing own learning and projects
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Manages their own learning and projects well, working alone and with others.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates manage their own learning and projects well, alone and with others.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will manage your own learning and projects well, on your own and with others.

statements.about: principles of ethical research
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can understand and use the principles of ethical research.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can understand and apply the principles of research ethics.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will understand the principles of ethical research and put them into practice.

statements.about: organising and using evidence from primary and secondary sources
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Organises and uses evidence, data and information from a range of primary and secondary sources.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates organise and use evidence, data and information drawn from varied primary and secondary sources.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will organise and use evidence, data and information from many kinds of original and secondary sources.

statements.about: personal integrity and the ethics of decisions
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can see why personal integrity matters and is aware of the ethical effects decisions may have.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can see why personal integrity matters and recognise the ethical effects that decisions may have.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will understand why personal integrity matters and be aware of the ethical consequences decisions can have.

statements.about: using constructive feedback
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Understands and uses constructive feedback.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand and act on constructive feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will understand constructive feedback and act on it.

statements.about: communication, information and data tools and software
statements.paraphrase: Threshold (the minimum for the award): Can choose and use suitable aids and software for communication, information and data analysis.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates can choose and use suitable aids and software for communicating, handling information and analysing data.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard for your honours degree, you will choose and use the right tools and software for communicating, handling information and analysing data.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: consistent, detailed knowledge of concepts, theories, evidence and issues
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows consistent and detailed knowledge of the main concepts and theories and awareness of current evidence and issues.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show consistent, detailed knowledge of the core concepts and theories and awareness of current evidence and debates.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will show detailed, consistent knowledge of the main concepts and theories and a good grasp of current evidence and debates.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: systematic, critical awareness of current problems and insights
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows systematic knowledge and understanding, and a critical awareness, of present problems or new insights, much of it from leading work in the discipline or practice.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show systematic knowledge and a critical awareness of current problems or new insights, much of it from leading research or practice.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will show a systematic and critical grasp of today's problems and new thinking in the field, much of it from leading research or practice.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: sophisticated collaboration towards shared goals
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Collaborates with others in a sophisticated way to reach shared aims, for instance in group work, projects and presentations.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will collaborate skilfully with others towards shared aims, for instance in group work, projects and presentations.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will work with others skilfully to reach shared aims, for example in group projects and presentations.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: developed communication in varied formats and for varied audiences
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Communicates with developed skill in formats suited to the context and to varied audiences.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will communicate with developed skill in formats suited to the context and the audience.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will communicate with real skill in forms that fit the setting and the people you are addressing.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: strong reasoned argument with critical judgement
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows a strong capacity to build reasoned arguments, drawing relevant information together and judging critically.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show a strong capacity to build reasoned arguments that draw information together and judge it critically.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will build strong, well-reasoned arguments that pull the relevant information together and weigh it critically.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: critical reflection on own learning
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows a developed capacity to reflect critically on their own learning.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show a developed capacity to reflect critically on how they learn.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will reflect critically and in depth on your own learning.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: effective handling of complex issues with incomplete data
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Handles complex issues effectively, in an orderly and inventive way, reaching sound judgements when data are incomplete.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will handle complex issues effectively, methodically and inventively, judging soundly when information is incomplete.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will handle complex issues effectively, methodically and creatively, and make sound judgements when information is missing.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: confident, creative problem-solving
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Finds, looks into and resolves problems with confidence, thinking creatively in practical and theoretical settings.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will find, examine and resolve problems with confidence, thinking creatively in practice and theory.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will find, look into and solve problems with confidence, thinking creatively in practice and in theory.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: excellent judgement of data approaches
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows an excellent capacity to judge and use suitable ways of gathering, analysing and presenting data.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show an excellent capacity to assess and use methods for gathering, analysing and presenting data.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will judge and use methods for gathering, analysing and presenting data to an excellent standard.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: timely, critical management of own learning and projects
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Manages their own learning and projects effectively, on time and critically, alone and with others.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will manage their learning and projects effectively, on time and critically, alone and with others.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will manage your learning and projects well, on time and with a critical eye, on your own and with others.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: clear grasp and use of research ethics
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Understands and uses the principles of ethical research with clarity.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will understand and apply research ethics with clarity.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will understand research ethics clearly and apply them with care.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: effective organisation and use of evidence from varied sources
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Organises and uses evidence, data and information from a range of primary and secondary sources effectively.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will organise and use evidence, data and information from varied primary and secondary sources effectively.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will organise and use evidence, data and information from many original and secondary sources effectively.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: evident grasp of integrity and the ethics of decisions
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows a clear understanding of why personal integrity matters and an awareness of the ethical effects decisions may have.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show a clear grasp of why personal integrity matters and of the ethical effects decisions may have.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will show a clear grasp of why personal integrity matters and of the ethical consequences of decisions.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: academic practice and professional behaviour
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Evaluates analytically, where relevant, how academic practice relates to professional conduct.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will evaluate analytically, where relevant, how academic practice relates to professional conduct.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will weigh up analytically, where it applies, how academic work relates to how professionals behave.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: developed use of constructive feedback
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows a developed understanding and use of constructive feedback.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show a developed understanding and use of constructive feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will understand constructive feedback well and use it to improve your work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at an excellent level
statements.about: strong choice and use of tools and software
statements.paraphrase: Excellent level (will): Shows a strong capacity to choose and use suitable aids and software for communication, information and data analysis.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show a strong capacity to choose and use aids and software for communication, information handling and data analysis.

forBeneficiary.text: At an excellent level, you will choose and use the right tools and software for communication, information and data analysis with real skill.

statements.about: specialist command and independent project work
statements.paraphrase: Master's graduates in the subject are expected to show graduate outcomes, command of at least one specialist area and independence in project work.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show graduate outcomes, command of at least one specialist area and independent project-based work.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will show that you command at least one specialist area and can carry out project work independently.

statements.about: public sector organisations, their context and management
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Understands systematically and in depth what is known about public sector organisations, their surroundings and how they are run.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a systematic, deep understanding of public sector organisations, their context and their management.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will understand public sector organisations, their setting and how they are managed, systematically and in depth.

statements.about: techniques for investigation, research and evaluation
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Understands fully and in detail the techniques for close investigation, research and evaluation, or advanced scholarship, in the field.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a full, detailed understanding of the techniques used for close investigation, research and evaluation, or advanced scholarship, in the field.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will understand fully the techniques for detailed investigation, research and evaluation in the field.

statements.about: proactive, independent learning
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Shows a proactive and independent approach to learning.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a proactive, independent approach to learning.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will take charge of your learning, proactively and independently.

statements.about: agile, reflexive and innovative learning
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Shows an agile, reflexive and inventive approach to learning.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show an agile, reflexive and inventive approach to learning.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will learn in a flexible, reflexive and inventive way.

statements.about: critical awareness of current issues
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Is critically and subtly aware of current issues, drawing on research and practice.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a critical, nuanced awareness of current issues, grounded in research and practice.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will have a critical, nuanced awareness of current issues, grounded in research and practice.

statements.about: critically evaluating research and scholarship
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Has the conceptual competence to evaluate current research and advanced scholarship critically.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show the conceptual competence to evaluate current research and advanced scholarship critically.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will have the conceptual tools to evaluate current research and advanced scholarship critically.

statements.about: applying knowledge to complex situations
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Applies relevant knowledge to a variety of complex situations, allowing for the field's mixed public, private and non-profit setting.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show the ability to apply relevant knowledge to varied complex situations, allowing for the field's hybrid setting.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will apply what you know to many complex situations, allowing for the mix of public, private and non-profit settings in the field.

statements.about: originality, creativity and entrepreneurship with research techniques
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Applies knowledge with originality, creativity and entrepreneurship, and understands in practice how established research techniques produce and interpret knowledge.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show originality, creativity and entrepreneurship in applying knowledge, and a practical grasp of how established research techniques produce and interpret knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will apply what you know with originality, creativity and enterprise, and understand in practice how research methods create and interpret knowledge.

statements.about: integrating theory, practice and experience
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Can assess and combine theory, practice and experience across many situations.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will assess and combine theory, practice and experience across many situations.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will assess and combine theory, practice and experience in many kinds of situation.

statements.about: how research and practice extend knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Understands fully how research and practice push forward the limits of knowledge.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a full understanding of how research and practice push forward the limits of knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will understand fully how research and practice push knowledge forward.

statements.about: public sector values, ethics and integrity
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Understands, and is committed to, the values and ethics of public service, and sees why acting with integrity and encouraging it in others matters.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a developed grasp of, and commitment to, the values and ethics of public service, acting with integrity and encouraging it in others.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will understand and commit to public sector values and ethics, and act with integrity and encourage it in others.

statements.about: professional reflection
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Has professional reflective capacities that improve professional practice.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show professional reflective capacities that improve professional practice.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will reflect as a professional in ways that improve your practice.

statements.about: effects of policy and administration on societies and the environment
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Understands, with nuance, how policy and administration affect societies and the environment.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show a nuanced understanding of how policy and administration affect societies and the environment.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will understand, with nuance, how policy and administration affect people, societies and the environment.

statements.about: an international and global perspective
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Can take an international and global view.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will take an international and global view.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will look at questions from an international and global point of view.

statements.about: collaborative, diverse working and leadership
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Can work, engage and lead in collaborative, multicultural and diverse settings at home and abroad.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will work, engage and lead in collaborative, multicultural and diverse settings at home and abroad.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will work, engage and lead in collaborative, multicultural and diverse settings, in the UK and internationally.

statements.about: negotiation and influence
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Can negotiate and influence in professional settings.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will negotiate and influence in professional settings.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will negotiate and influence others in professional settings.

statements.about: independent learning for continuing professional development
statements.paraphrase: Master's level (will): Has the independent learning ability needed for continuing professional development.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, graduates will show the independent learning ability needed for continuing professional development.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's in this subject, you will have the independent learning ability you need to keep developing professionally.
